[1/4] Evaluate all 227 Blocked aikit revisit conditions against live evidence

impact_assessment.why: 227 of 365 aikit ideas sit Blocked behind an explicit revisit condition, and nothing has ever re-evaluated those conditions. Some are now provably true (IDEA-955's own trigger: a gate silently stopped firing), so the block is stale and the backlog overstates what is closed.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every Blocked idea gets an evidence-backed verdict: the condition fired and it reopens, or it is still unmet and stays blocked with a dated check. The register stops claiming closure it cannot support.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: .idea-catcher/ideas.json status, tags and review_log; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: another session holds uncommitted Track C edits in tests/ and the map; state: ideas.json and the task ledger
impact_assessment.mitigation: write only under .idea-catcher/ (gitignored) so the other session's files are untouched; every unblock goes through review-idea with cited evidence; conditions that need judgement stay blocked

[1/3] Deep-verify non-Blocked ideas: subsumption claims, not just symbol presence

impact_assessment.why: The previous pass tagged 138 non-blocked aikit ideas by symbol existence and status. That is too weak: a Superseded idea can point at a successor that only half-covers it, and a Rejected 'already implemented' claim can drift. Two subsumption claims are now proven partial.
impact_assessment.benefits: Superseded and Rejected rows carry a verdict grounded in exercised behaviour, so the register stops asserting coverage it does not have.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: .idea-catcher tags and history; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: another session holds Track C edits in tests/ and the map; state: ideas.json and the task ledger
impact_assessment.mitigation: probe each claim by running the mechanism; write only under .idea-catcher/; keep disputed where a successor covers only part of the idea

[1/5] Discover implicit state machines the 19-machine registry misses

impact_assessment.why: scripts/state_machines.py already encodes 19 lifecycles as data, but implicit machines remain wherever a lifecycle is tracked in JSON fields, strings or files without an entry. A registry that claims to be the readable list while missing machines is worse than none: a reader trusts it as complete.
impact_assessment.benefits: The registry becomes the actual inventory, so the same lifecycle cannot be re-derived differently in a second module; the gaps the entries record become visible to UX/DX/AX at once.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: scripts/state_machines.py data, the --check-status CLI, knowledge/state_machines.md; dependency: none (stdlib only); concurrency: another session holds uncommitted tests/ and codebase_map.md edits; state: state_machines.py, its tests, the knowledge page, the map
impact_assessment.mitigation: discover by scanning for status vocabularies and compare against the registry; add entries as data only; prove each new entry against the real code; run the full gate set and both tiers before commit
